2027-03-09.title: Tuesday of the fifth week of the Great Fast · The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste
readings: “The Lord will provide”: the ram in place of Isaac
Completing what is lacking in Christ's afflictions for the sake of his body
Take up your cross and follow me
2027-03-09.alt: Great Fast (Valiya Nombu), fifth week. Commemoration of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste.
2027-03-09.verse: He called the crowd with his disciples, and said to them, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.
theo: Yesterday we left Abraham and Isaac walking up the mountain together. Today the story reaches its summit. “Abraham built an altar there and laid the wood in order. He bound his son Isaac, and laid him on the altar, on top of the wood.” At the last moment the angel calls: “Do not lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him; for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.” Abraham sees a ram caught in a thicket and offers it “instead of his son,” and he names the place “The Lord will provide.” God then swears by himself: “by your offspring shall all the nations of the earth gain blessing for themselves, because you have obeyed my voice.” St Paul hears the echo of this chapter when he writes: “He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?” Isaac was spared; the Son of God was not. Tradition places Moriah where the Temple later stood, near the hill where Christ was crucified, so that the mountain of the test became the mountain of the gift.

In the Gospel Jesus speaks openly of that gift: “the Son of Man must undergo great suffering, and be rejected… and be killed, and after three days rise again.” Peter, who had just confessed him as the Messiah, takes him aside to rebuke him, and Jesus answers: “Get behind me, Satan! For you are setting your mind not on divine things but on human things.” Then he speaks to all: “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.” Today the Church remembers forty soldiers who did exactly that. At Sebaste in Armenia, around the year 320, under the emperor Licinius, forty Christian soldiers refused to sacrifice to idols. They were left naked through a winter night on a frozen lake, with a warm bath-house on the shore for anyone who would deny Christ. One gave up and ran to the bath; a guard, seeing the faith of the others, took off his own clothes and joined them, so that forty still stood on the ice. St Basil the Great, preaching on their feast, imagined them praying: the winter is bitter, but paradise is sweet; the frost is painful, but the rest that follows is blessed (in substance). St Paul gives the meaning of such suffering: “I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ's afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church.” Nothing is lacking in Christ's sacrifice; what remains is for his members to share in it, so that his love reaches every place and age.
outline: Ask: what would make me turn back on a cold night?
Point 1 · On the mount of the Lord
The ram in Isaac's place; the Son not withheld.
Peter's human thinking and the way of Jesus.
Completing what is lacking for the sake of the Church.
“Let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.”
live: Name one thing you have kept back from God this Lent and offer it to him today in prayer.
Accept one discomfort today without complaint and unite it to Christ for someone who is suffering.
2027-03-09.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, the Father did not withhold you from us but gave you up for us all, and on the mountain of the Lord he provided the Lamb. You call us to deny ourselves, take up our cross and follow you. By the prayers of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste, who stood firm through the frozen night, give us courage not to turn back toward easy comfort, and let our small sufferings serve your body, the Church. Amen.
altar: The sacrifice that Abraham was spared, the Father offered in his Son; at the altar of the Holy Qurbono we share in it and receive the strength of the martyrs.

quick: The angel stopped Abraham's hand; a ram was offered instead of Isaac, and the place was called “The Lord will provide.”
Jesus foretold his Passion and called all who follow him to deny themselves and take up their cross.
The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste chose a frozen lake over denying Christ.
2027-03-09.action: Accept one discomfort today in silence and offer it for someone who suffers.
2027-03-09.question: What is the warm bath-house on the shore that tempts me to leave Christ?

family.explain: Jesus says that to follow him we must carry our cross. Long ago forty soldiers at Sebaste stood all night on a frozen lake because they would not stop loving Jesus. One gave up, but a guard came and took his place. We can carry small crosses too: being kind when we are tired, sharing when we want to keep.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith today.
family.ask: Ask: “What small cross can each of us carry this week?”

illus: In a hostel in Delhi a girl from Kollam was the only one on her floor who went to Holy Qurbono on Sunday mornings. The others slept late and teased her as she left in the cold. One January morning she nearly stayed in bed; the room was warm, the road outside was foggy, and no one would know. She went. Some weeks later a quiet girl from another state, who had never spoken to her, asked if she could come along. She said she had watched her go out every Sunday in the cold, and she wanted to see what was worth it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave yourself for us. Give us courage to take up our cross and follow you. Amen.
share: Now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son (Genesis 22:12). What am I holding back from God?
Let them deny themselves and take up their cross (Mark 8:34). Which cross am I trying to avoid?
I am completing what is lacking in Christ's afflictions (Colossians 1:24). How can my suffering become an offering for others?
pm.resp: Lord, strengthen us to follow you.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith in our time.
For soldiers, police and all who serve in harsh conditions.
For those tempted to give up their faith for comfort or advancement.
For the sick, that they may unite their pain to the Cross of Christ.
For our parish, that we may persevere to the end of the Great Fast.
pm.close: Father, you did not withhold your only Son but gave him up for us all. By the prayers of the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste make us faithful to death, that we may receive the crown of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on the mountain Abraham bound Isaac and laid him on the wood. Then the angel called: do not lay your hand on the boy; for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me (Genesis 22:12). A ram was offered in his place, and the place was named: The Lord will provide.

St Paul tells us what God provided: he who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us (Romans 8:32). Isaac came down the mountain alive; Jesus went up Calvary and gave his life, and on the third day he rose.

When Jesus spoke of his Passion, Peter tried to stop him, and Jesus said: you are setting your mind not on divine things but on human things. If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me (Mark 8:33–34).

Today we remember the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste, who stood through a winter night on a frozen lake rather than deny Christ. When one fell away, a guard took his place. Paul says: I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake (Colossians 1:24). May their prayers help us carry our cross to the end of this Fast. Amen.
kids: Children, God stopped Abraham and gave a ram instead of Isaac. But God the Father gave us his own Son, Jesus, because he loves us so much. Today we remember forty brave soldiers who stood all night on ice because they loved Jesus. When something is hard this week, say: Jesus, I carry this with you.

intro: Theme: “Let them deny themselves and take up their cross and follow me.”
The ram in Isaac's place, the Son the Father did not withhold, and the Forty Martyrs who would not turn back.

points.h: On the mount of the Lord
sub: A ram instead of his son.
The Son who was not withheld.
q: Sacrifice and offering you do not desire, but you have given me an open ear. Burnt offering and sin offering you have not required.
He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?
points.apply: Thank the Father tonight for one gift that came to you through the Cross.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
For this slight momentary affliction is preparing us for an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure,
points.apply: Accept one daily discomfort this week without complaint, for Christ.

sub: The guard who took the empty place.
q: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
points.apply: Pray this week for one Christian community that suffers for the faith.

concl: God provided the Lamb on the mountain; Christ invites us to share his Cross.
The martyrs show that no comfort is worth more than fidelity to Christ.
2027-03-09.resolve: Carry one hidden cross daily for the rest of the Fast, offered for the persecuted Church.
